# Mermaid ASCII terminal test assets

Upstream: https://github.com/AlexanderGrooff/mermaid-ascii

Release: `1.6.1`; commit `5f00e3d9ac9fc96a19859d502333e35b87d2ffea`.
All assets are MIT licensed; the full upstream license is in `LICENSE`.

## What is preserved

- All 32 original Go test files, including complete assertion text and two seeded
  fuzz functions, plus the original test-only golden-file helper.
- All 321 original golden files: graph 92 ASCII, 47 Unicode, three multibyte;
  sequence 39 ASCII and 57 Unicode; ER 13 ASCII and 70 Unicode.
- `provenance.json`: exact source file hashes, byte lengths and release pin.
- `test_inventory.json`: all 162 Test/Example/Fuzz functions and explicit public
  drawing, golden driver, parser, private-model and configuration/helper scope.
- `cases.json`: 299 unique exact-byte inputs: 295 positive drawing cases, three
  error cases and one valid-empty ER case with a private/parser contract.

The imported input population includes public inline literals, all fuzz seeds,
and every finite generated public drawing source: a 30-node chain, a 15-edge ER
lane example, three self-loop name lengths, two Unicode cluster label values,
and all five fanout-label source variants. Foreign ASCII and padding permutations
remain explicit original assertions/provenance, not inflated distinct syntax
coverage. The standalone internal object-construction/control-byte test is kept
in the source inventory; it does not fabricate a public Mermaid input.

## Semantic expectations and known upstream losses

Every positive requires actual drawing; source fallback is a failure. Original
upstream expected outputs and options remain in `expectation.snapshots`, with
contains/not-contains facts and source predicates preserved separately.

All 295 positive inputs have `expectation.semantic_model` generated by the exact
release parser, using a scratch-only maintenance serializer. There are 296 parsed
models including the valid-empty case; all three parser errors correspond to the
explicit negative inputs. No Go parser, layout, renderer or serializer code is
vendored here, and native tests require no Go runtime or toolchain.

The parser models are supporting facts, not an excuse to copy known upstream
semantic losses:

- Go graph node specs normalize shape outlines.
- Its Unicode renderer loses dotted/thick edge distinctions and open/cross/circle
  endpoint distinctions that its ASCII renderer preserves.
- Its sequence actor declaration is normalized to a participant box.

Raw shape/operator/actor source remains available for stronger combined-suite
obligations. Preserve the more expressive semantics established by other pinned
terminal suites rather than weakening them to match these losses.

The corpus also includes literal control-byte and leading-combining-mark cases.
Original bytes and assertions remain intact. A native terminal port must explicitly
record safe visible-text corrections where raw control emission is unsuitable;
it must not silently emit terminal controls or count source fallback as drawing.

## Upstream execution evidence

The exact release ran under scratch Go 1.23.4: **862 passing test events, zero
failures**, comprising 162 top-level Test/Example/Fuzz functions and subtests.
There are 812 leaf test events and 50 parent events. Seven test packages passed;
the root package has no tests. Counts include helper/parser tests and therefore
must not be presented as 862 terminal drawing cases.

Log from the development run:
`build/mermaid-renderer-research-20261019/mermaid-ascii-1.6.1-upstream-tests.jsonl`.
These are upstream results, not a claim that Loom's native port passes them.
